parole.significato: An AGA cooker.
parole.testo: Genericized trademark of AGA AB. Unadapted borrowing from Swedish AGA; an abbreviation of Aktiebolaget Gasaccumulator, meaning "The stock company Gas Accumulator".

parole.significato: A limestone pavement.
parole.testo: From Swedish alvar (“alvar”), from alv (“subsoil”). Possibly related to Old High German Alp (“alpine pasture; alp”).

parole.significato: A unit of length equal to 10⁻¹⁰ meters (that is, one ten-billionth of a meter), approximately the size of an atom, and…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish ångström, named after Swedish physicist Anders Jonas Ångström.

parole.significato: A Scandinavian liquor distilled from potato or grain mash to about 40% ABV and typically flavored with anise, although…
parole.testo: From Swedish and Danish akvavit and Norwegian akevitt, from Medieval Latin aqua vitae (“water of life”). Doublet of aqua vitae and akvavit. Compare eau de vie, whisky, whiskey, and water of life from the same source.

parole.significato: An alkaline lye which neutralizes the effect of the previous application of lime, and makes hides supple in the process…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish beta (“maceration, tanning”).

parole.significato: A plush toy in the form of a shark, especially one manufactured by the Swedish company IKEA.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish blåhaj (“blue shark”).

parole.significato: A style of modernist architecture characterized by angular geometry and overt signs of the construction process.
parole.testo: From brutal + -ism. Popularized in 1954 by the English architects Alison and Peter Smithson, from earlier Swedish nybrutalism (“New Brutalism”), after French béton brut (“raw concrete”), the material favored by Le Corbusier.

parole.significato: Any of various Nordic distilled liquors.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish brännvin. Doublet of brandywine.

parole.significato: The study of buttons (clothing fasteners and badges).
parole.testo: From button + -ology. In the sense of pedantic systematization, a calque of Swedish knappologi with the same literal meaning.

parole.significato: A soldier (or war veteran) of the Swedish kings Charles XI and Charles XII.
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish karolin, ultimately derived from Latin Carolus (“Charles”).

parole.significato: Relating to the metric temperature scale of said name.
parole.testo: Named after Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius (1701–1744), who first proposed the centigrade scale in 1742. The surname is Latinized from the estate's name, Latin celsus (“mound”).

parole.significato: A genre of Swedish popular music influenced by rock and roll, schlager and other styles.
parole.testo: From Swedish dansband (“dance band”).

parole.significato: A veal stew in dill sauce.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish dillkött.

parole.significato: A style of tracker music influenced by disco and associated with the demoscene.
parole.testo: From dosk - onomatopoeic of the punchy sound of drums and bass lines + pop. It was later interpreted as a backronym from Swedish disco och synth-kombinerad pop (disco and synth combined pop). https://web.archive.org/web/20181207142300/http://www.spacesynth.net/Interview/GustafGrefberg

parole.significato: An athletic training technique, used especially in running, in which periods of intense effort alternate with periods o…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish fartlek, from fart (“speed”) + lek (“child’s play”).

parole.significato: The Swedish practice of taking a break from daily activities or meeting with people to enjoy pastries and drinks, typic…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish fika.

parole.significato: A Nordic dairy product, similar to yogurt, but using different bacteria which give a different taste and texture.
parole.testo: From Swedish fil, a clipping of filmjölk. Also related to Finnish viili.

parole.significato: the Swedish language as spoken by the Swedish-speaking population in Finland
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish finlandssvenska.

parole.significato: Of or pertaining to native Swedish-speakers living in Finland
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish finlandssvensk.

parole.significato: A more or less open body of water in a coastal archipelago.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish fjärd. Doublet of fjord, ford, port, and firth.

parole.significato: A depression or hollow within a bog.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish flark (“bog or swamp overgrown with tufts of grass; clearing in a bog with more water and less vegetation than its surroundings”).

parole.significato: The monetary unit of Sweden between the 15th and 17th centuries, valued at between one-sixth and one-half of an öre.
parole.testo: From Swedish fyrk, from Middle Low German vêreken, from ver/vier (“four”).

parole.significato: A chemical element (symbol Gd) with atomic number 64: a ductile silvery-white metal.
parole.testo: Named after chemist Johan Gadolin, a Swedish-speaking Finn, + -ium.

parole.significato: The military punishment known as running the gauntlet.
parole.testo: From Swedish gatlopp, from Swedish gata (“street, lane”) + lopp (“course, run”). Compare German Gassenlaufen.

parole.significato: Two parallel rows of attackers who strike at a criminal as punishment.
parole.testo: Modified, under the influence of etymology 1, from gantlope, from Swedish gatlopp (“passageway”), from Old Swedish gata (“lane”) + lopp (“course”), from löpa (“to run”) ]

parole.significato: The study of the effects of geography (especially economic geography) on politics and international relations, usually…
parole.testo: From geo- + politics, calque of Swedish geopolitik, coined in 1900 by Rudolf Kjellén.

parole.significato: A Scandinavian version of vin chaud or mulled wine; a hot punch made of red wine, brandy and sherry flavoured with almo…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish glögg.

parole.significato: Salmon dry-cured in salt, seasoned with dill and sugar, and served usually thinly sliced as an appetizer.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish gravlax, a compound of grava (“to dry-cure in salt and sugar”) + lax (“salmon”).

parole.significato: A mud formed from the partial decay of peat.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish.

parole.significato: A type of metamorphic rock, formed from volcanic tuff and rich in quartz and feldspars.
parole.testo: From Swedish hälleflinta.

parole.significato: A handrail, especially one fitted on one side of a planked or wooden bridge.
parole.testo: Compare dialectal Swedish hammel (“little bar or beam”).

parole.significato: A fine-grained rock consisting of an intimate mixture of quartz and feldspar, sometimes banded or striated, sometimes c…
parole.testo: From Swedish hälleflinta (literally “rock-flint”), from häll + flinta (compare Old Norse flettu (grjót (“flintstone”)), from Middle Low German vlint, from Old Saxon *flint, from Proto-West Germanic *flint).

parole.significato: A phonetic feature found in Swedish, a form of rounding where the lips are protruded and kept relatively close together.
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish inrundning.

parole.significato: A breed of dog of the spitz type that is found in Northern Europe, eponymous with Jämtland.
parole.testo: From Swedish, named after Jämtland (derives from its inhabitants, the Jamts) + hund (“dog”).

parole.significato: A type of beef stew.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish kalops from English collops.

parole.significato: An old Swedish unit of area, equivalent to 154.3 m² (1,661 sq ft).
parole.testo: From Swedish kappland, from kappe (“designation for space measure”) (see kapa (“to cut in lengths”)) + land.

parole.significato: Synonym of nyckelharpa.
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish nyckelharpa

parole.significato: A soft wax used for grip on skis, especially for corn snow or crust.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish klister.

parole.significato: A kind of strong, smooth brown wrapping paper.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish kraft (“strength”) as used in kraftpapper. Doublet of craft.

parole.significato: A slightly sweet Scandinavian cookie usually shaped as a figure eight.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Swedish kringla (“pretzel”) for the cookie's pretzel-like shape.

parole.significato: The official currency of Sweden.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish krona (“crown”). Doublet of corona, crown, korona, koruna, króna, and krone.

parole.significato: Waterlogged, marshy area around the perimeter of a (raised) bog, where water collects.
parole.testo: Most likely from Swedish lagg (“moist, marshy area around a bog”), though compare the dialectal (Sussex, Somerset) English term(s) lag ("long, narrow, marshy meadow, usually by the side of a stream") and leg ("long, narrow meadow, gen. one which runs out of a larger piece of land"), apparently from

parole.significato: In medieval Scandinavia and parts of the Danelaw: a district official, magistrate or judge; a lawspeaker.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish lagman. Doublet of lawman.

parole.significato: The philosophy or ethos of trying to achieve balance in one's life.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish lagom (“just right”).

parole.significato: A province in various Scandinavian countries.
parole.testo: From Swedish landskap.

parole.significato: An indigenous person from Lapland. One of the Sami people.
parole.testo: From Swedish lapp, possibly of Finnish origin. Compare Finnish Lappi.

parole.significato: A type of spitz, traditionally used to herd reindeer
parole.testo: From Swedish lapphund, from lapp (“Lapp”) + hund (“dog”).

parole.significato: An aggregation of male animals for the purposes of courtship and display.
parole.testo: From Germanic roots meaning "play". In the biology sense, it comes specifically from Swedish lek (“child's play”), by means of Swedish leka (“to play”). The verb is first attested in English in 1871 and the noun at least as early as 1867.

parole.significato: Swedish-style rye bread made with molasses.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish limpa (“loaf [of bread]”).

parole.significato: A type of physiotherapy designed to promote health through exercise and massage.
parole.testo: From mechano- + therapy, after Swedish mekanoterapi.

parole.significato: Any rock of mixed appearance, being an intimate mixture of granite and older rock, specifically from intense metamorphi…
parole.testo: From Swedish migmatit, from Ancient Greek μίγμα (mígma, “mixture”) + Swedish -it (“-ite”).

parole.significato: Any semi-aquatic, carnivorous mammal in the Mustelinae subfamily, similar to weasels, with dark fur, native to Europe a…
parole.testo: From Late Middle English mynk (“fur of the European mink”), apparently from Swedish mink, mänk, menk (“stinking animal in Finland, mink”). Compare Danish mink (“mink”), Icelandic minkur (“mink”).

parole.significato: Any of several species of large pelagic petrels and fulmars, such as Fulmarus glacialis of the North Atlantic and sever…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish mallemucke (“stormy petrel”).

parole.significato: A test of the stability of a vehicle, which determines the maximum speed it can attain and still be able to steer clear…
parole.testo: From Swedish älgtest (which see for more), from German Elchtest; although a Swedish test, the word was coined in German and then calqued into Swedish.

parole.significato: A lightweight, two-wheeled vehicle equipped with a small motor and pedals, designed to go no faster than some specified…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish moped.

parole.significato: A kind of small sheath knife.
parole.testo: Swedish morakniv, as originally made in Mora, Dalarna, Sweden.

parole.significato: A dicarboxylic acid, HOOC-(CHOH)₄-COOH, produced by the oxidation of the milk sugar galactose, used as a test for the p…
parole.testo: From Swedish mjölk-socker-syra (milk-sugar-acid).

parole.significato: The soul of a dead but unbaptized child that roams the Earth.
parole.testo: From Swedish myling.

parole.significato: A Nobel Prize.
parole.testo: From Swedish Nobel.

parole.significato: A small to medium-sized breed with typical spitz-like features, traditionally kept as a hunting dog in northern Sweden.
parole.testo: From Swedish, from Norrbotten + spets (“spitz”).

parole.significato: A string instrument (chordophone) with a long body and a boat-shaped soundbox, with keys attached to tangents that act…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish nyckelharpa.

parole.significato: An old Swedish unit of weight.
parole.testo: Swedish nyläst

parole.significato: A small island.
parole.testo: From Swedish ö and Danish ø. Doublet of ey.

parole.significato: An appointed official whose duty is to investigate complaints, generally on behalf of individuals such as consumers or…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish ombudsman (equivalent to ombud (“representative, proxy”) + man), from Old Norse umboðsmaðr.

parole.significato: Someone who takes part in the sport of orienteering.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish orientera.

parole.significato: The act of racing across unfamiliar place using a map and compass.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish orientering, from orientera (“orient, orientate”) + -ing.

parole.significato: An osar or esker.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish ås.

parole.significato: An esker.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish åsar.

parole.significato: A Swedish dessert made from curdled milk.
parole.testo: From Swedish ostkaka.

parole.significato: A phonetic feature found in Swedish, a form of rounding where the lips are protruded and kept relatively far apart.
parole.testo: A calque of Swedish utrundning.

parole.significato: Needle ice; ice structures formed when the air temperature is below 0℃ and the soil is not.
parole.testo: From Swedish pipkrake, from pip (“tube”) + krake (“thin, fine, weak”), coined by Swedish botanist Henrik Hesselman in 1907.

parole.significato: A person, especially a girl or woman, with long or flamboyant red hair, especially in pigtails or parted down the middl…
parole.testo: From long + stocking, calque of Swedish Pippi Långstrump. As a common noun, after the appearance and nature of the fictional character.

parole.significato: jogging and picking up litter
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish plogging, coined in 2016 as blend of plocka upp (“to pick up”) and jogging (“jogging”). From there the practice has spread to other countries.

parole.significato: A Swedish layer cake with layers of airy sponge, pastry cream, and whipped cream, covered in usually green marzipan.
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish prinsesstårta.

parole.significato: A left-wing, anticommercial musical movement in Sweden in the 1960s and 1970s.
parole.testo: Swedish, a contraction of progressiv musik (“progressive music”).

parole.significato: A Swedish fruit liqueur based on Batavia arrack, neutral spirits, and flavorings.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish punsch, from English punch.

parole.significato: Someone who is part of a subculture in Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Belgium and the Netherla…
parole.testo: From Swedish raggare, from ragga (“to drive around”), from dialectal term raga (“to stagger”).

parole.significato: A unit of currency that was used in Sweden between 1777 and 1873.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish riksdaler.

parole.significato: A variety of the Swedish language used by immigrants in the Swedish capital of Stockholm, especially in the suburb of R…
parole.testo: From Rinkeby + Swedish. Calque of Swedish rinkebysvenska.

parole.significato: The swede, or Swedish turnip; the European plant Brassica napus var. napobrassica
parole.testo: First attested in 1799, borrowed from Swedish rotabagge, a dialectal word from Västergötland, from rot (“root”) + bagge (“lump, bunch”).

parole.significato: A Scandinavian knotted-pile woollen rug, used as bed-cover and tapestry.
parole.testo: From Swedish rya (“thick cloth”).

parole.significato: A Saab car or plane.
parole.testo: Initialism of Swedish Svenska Aeroplan Aktiebolaget (“Swedish Aeroplane Company”).

parole.significato: Synonym of ammonia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish salmiak. Doublet of salmiac.

parole.significato: A young gull.
parole.testo: From Swedish [Term?].

parole.significato: To scamper off.
parole.testo: Origin unknown; perhaps from scut(tle), or related to Swedish skutta (“to leap”).

parole.significato: A pastry with a cream and almond paste filling, traditionally eaten on Shrove Tuesday in Sweden, Finland and Estonia.
parole.testo: From Swedish semla, ultimately from Latin simila (“finest quality wheat flour”), through Old Swedish. Doublet of semola and semel; compare semolina.

parole.significato: In the International System of Units, the derived unit of radiation dose: the dose received in one hour at a distance o…
parole.testo: From Swedish Sievert. Named after the Swedish radiologist Rolf Sievert.

parole.significato: Any of various metamorphic rocks formed by metasomatism.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish skarn (“skarn, filth”), from Old Norse skarn, from Proto-Germanic *skarną. Doublet of sharn.

parole.significato: Slate.
parole.testo: Presumably Swedish skiffer.

parole.significato: A fictional creature, associated with an old Swedish hunting story, that is half hare and half wood grouse.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish skvader.

parole.significato: A Scandinavian system of handicraft-based education that emphasizes the importance of practical, hands-on work to devel…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish slöjd (“handicraft, handiwork, skills”). Doublet of sleight.

parole.significato: A system of handicraft-based education started in Finland in 1865 and later adopted worldwide.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish slöjd (“sleight of hand, skilled or crafty”), from Old Swedish sløghþ, from Old Norse slœgð, from Proto-Germanic *slōgiþō, from *slōgiz (“cunning”) (whence English sly). Doublet of sleight and sly.

parole.significato: A Swedish-style buffet comprising a variety of cold sandwiches and other dishes; (by extension) any buffet with a wide…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish smörgåsbord (“buffet with many small dishes; smorgasbord”), from smörgås (“sandwich”) + bord (“table”). Smörgås is from Swedish smör (“butter”) + gås (“goose”), a reference to pieces of butter which float to the surface of milk when churned.

parole.significato: A type of tobacco snuff consumed in the form of a moist powder which is placed under the (usually upper) lip, without c…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish snus.

parole.significato: An orthorhombic-dipyramidal mineral containing calcium, fluorine, oxygen, and phosphorus.
parole.testo: Swedish spodiosit, from Ancient Greek σπόδιος (spódios, “grey”).

parole.significato: A fledgling (young) bird.
parole.testo: Unknown. Possibly related to dialectal Swedish skvabb (“fatty, flabby”). First attested in the 17th century.

parole.significato: To suffer from Stockholm syndrome; to form an emotional bond or identification with one's captor or oppressor, also, to…
parole.testo: From Swedish Stockholm, compound of stock (“log”) + holme (“islet”), possibly referring to logs put outside of the Stockholm shores to prevent ships from invading.

parole.significato: A psychological condition in which a hostage emotionally bonds to their captor.
parole.testo: Calque of Swedish Norrmalmstorgssyndrom. Named after the robbery of Kreditbanken at the Norrmalmstorg square in Stockholm, Sweden, in which the bank robbers held bank employees hostage from August 23 to August 28, 1973. Originally, this term was directly translated from Swedish Norrmalmstorgssyndrom

parole.significato: A traditional Swedish food made by fermenting Baltic herring in wooden casks.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish surströmming, from sur (“sour”) + strömming (“Baltic herring”).

parole.significato: A non-SI unit of sedimentation rate (symbol S or Sv), the rate at which particles of a given size and shape travel to t…
parole.testo: From Swedish Svedberg. Named after the Swedish chemist Theodor Svedberg (1884–1971).

parole.significato: A dog of a small, powerful breed associated with the Vikings.
parole.testo: From Swedish + Swedish vallhund (“herding dog”), from valla (“herd”) + hund (“dog”).

parole.significato: A dark yellow resinous acidic oil obtained as a byproduct during the pulping of pine; it is used in the manufacture of…
parole.testo: From Swedish tallolja (“pine oil”).

parole.significato: A sheep (originally a ewe) in its second year, or from the time it is weaned until it is first shorn.
parole.testo: First used to contemptuously refer to a woman, then later applied to a ewe in her second year. Possibly borrowed from Swedish tacka (“ewe”).

parole.significato: frozen ground
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish tjäle, which is descended from Old Swedish *þiæli, from Old Norse þeli (“frozen ground”), which is related to þel (“nap on wool; underwool”), and ultimately from Proto-Germanic *þelą.

parole.significato: A small human-like creature in Nordic folklore that lives on farmsteads and watches over their inhabitants.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish tomte.

parole.significato: An edible fish, Brosme brosme.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish torsk.

parole.significato: A dark coloured igneous rock; (now usually) any nongranitic igneous rock.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish trapp (“step, stair, stairway”), from Middle Low German trappe (“stair, step”).

parole.significato: A rare metallic chemical element (symbol W, from Latin wolframium) with an atomic number of 74.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish tungsten (“scheelite”), from tung (“heavy”) + sten (“stone”).

parole.significato: Synonym of barrel of land.
parole.testo: Swedish tunnland.

parole.significato: An annual layer of sediment or sedimentary rock.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish varv (“layer”).

parole.significato: A motor car manufactured by Volvo.
parole.testo: From Swedish Volvo, from Latin volvō (“to roll”), in reference to ball bearings which were the company's original product.

parole.significato: A humanoid demon with the head, claws, and wings of a giant vulture.
parole.testo: Introduced in the Dungeons & Dragons role-playing game in the 1970s. Possibly related to Swedish vråk (“buzzard”).

parole.significato: The state of a nucleus with minimum energy, but excluding the yrast. The second-least excited state for a given angular…
parole.testo: From Swedish yrare.

parole.significato: The state of a nucleus with minimum energy (i.e. when least excited) for a given angular momentum.
parole.testo: From Swedish yrast.

parole.significato: Any of several minerals, aluminosilicates of sodium, potassium, calcium or magnesium, that have a porous structure (ori…
parole.testo: From Swedish zeolit, and its source, New Latin zeolites, from Ancient Greek ζέω (zéō, “to boil, bubble”) + -lite.

parole.significato: An evaporite, consisting of mixture of sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate, Na₃HCO₃CO₃·2H₂O.
parole.testo: From Swedish trona or from Spanish trona, both derived from Arabic أَطْرُون (ʔaṭrūn), from نَطْرُون (naṭrūn), from Ancient Greek νίτρον (nítron), ultimately from Egyptian nṯrj: R9. Doublet of natron and niter.
